titulo: Prueba de Acceso a la Universidad 2027 — Lengua Extranjera II: Inglés — Castilla y León
instrucciones: Duración: 90 minutos. Puntuación total: 10 puntos. Lee el texto y responde a las preguntas 1–4. Contesta en inglés y sigue las indicaciones de cada apartado. En la pregunta 5, elige y redacta solo una de las dos opciones en 120–150 palabras.

preguntas.enunciado:
READ THE TEXT CAREFULLY, THEN ANSWER THE QUESTIONS BELOW.

THE LIBRARY THAT LENDS MORE THAN BOOKS

At Eastmere Public Library, visitors can borrow more than books. The Borrowing Bench is a collection of household tools, sports equipment and kitchen items that local residents can take home for a short time. Librarian Priya Shah came up with the idea after visitors repeatedly asked where they could borrow things such as a drill or a sewing machine. Buying an item for a single job could be expensive, she realised, and many people had little room to store it.

The library used a small local grant to buy 40 durable tools. Residents from nearby streets donated sports gear and kitchen equipment. The project began as a six-month pilot, and 240 households registered during that period. Members may borrow up to two items at a time for seven days, free of charge.

The library wants people to use the equipment safely. Every item comes with illustrated instructions, and volunteer repairers give free 20-minute demonstrations on the first Saturday of each month. The library does not accept unsafe or broken donations; volunteers inspect donated items before they are added to the collection.

A survey of members found that 78% had completed a household task they had previously put off because they did not have the right equipment. Some library staff initially worried that the project would create extra work, but volunteers now help check items in and out, while staff maintain the online catalogue. The library hopes to continue the scheme and make practical equipment accessible to more people.

1) ARE THE FOLLOWING STATEMENTS TRUE OR FALSE? JUSTIFY YOUR ANSWER BY CITING THE CORRESPONDING WORDS OR SENTENCES OF THE TEXT (2 POINTS; 0.5 POINTS EACH).

a) The idea for the Borrowing Bench came from the town council.

b) Members can borrow a maximum of two items for seven days.

c) The library accepts broken equipment if volunteers inspect it.

d) Most of the members surveyed said they had completed a task they had previously postponed.
preguntas.solucion:
### Resolución paso a paso
Se identifica en cada caso la afirmación del texto que trata el mismo asunto y se compara con lo que afirma el enunciado.

1. **a) FALSE.** El texto atribuye la idea a la bibliotecaria: *Librarian Priya Shah came up with the idea*. Por tanto, no surgió del ayuntamiento.
2. **b) TRUE.** El texto dice: *Members may borrow up to two items at a time for seven days*. Esto confirma el máximo de dos artículos simultáneos y el plazo de siete días.
3. **c) FALSE.** El texto afirma: *The library does not accept unsafe or broken donations* y explica que los voluntarios inspeccionan los artículos donados antes de incorporarlos. La inspección no significa que acepten artículos rotos.
4. **d) TRUE.** El 78 % completó una tarea que había aplazado: *78% had completed a household task they had previously put off*. Como el 78 % es más de la mitad, se trata de la mayoría.

**Comprobación final:** las respuestas son FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE. Cada una está respaldada por una cita pertinente del texto; con 0,5 puntos por apartado, la puntuación es **2/2**.
preguntas.resultado: a) FALSE; b) TRUE; c) FALSE; d) TRUE. Nota: 2/2.
preguntas.criterios: 0,5 puntos por apartado, hasta 2 puntos. En cada uno se valora la identificación correcta de TRUE/FALSE y su justificación con información o una cita pertinente del texto; sin justificación textual, no se concede la puntuación completa.

preguntas.enunciado:
SELECT AND WRITE THE COMPOSITION THAT YOU PREFER FROM THE FOLLOWING OPTIONS. USE BETWEEN 120–150 WORDS (3 POINTS).

a) Some people think public libraries should lend useful objects as well as books. Do you agree? Give reasons and examples to support your opinion.

b) Write an email to your school’s student council proposing a clothes-swap event for students. Explain how it could work and why it might be useful.
preguntas.solucion:
### 1. Elección y enfoque
Elijo la opción **b)**. En lugar de organizar el texto como una opinión general, empleo la estructura práctica de una propuesta: problema, funcionamiento del intercambio y beneficios.

### 2. Composición
**Subject: Clothes swap event**

Dear Student Council,

I would like to suggest a clothes swap at school. Many students own clothes they no longer wear, even though they are still in good condition. Rather than throwing them away, we could let someone else use them.

The event could be held in the gym after classes on a Friday. Each student could bring up to five clean items. Volunteers would check and sort the clothes by size. Students would receive one token for every item accepted, then use their tokens to choose other clothes. Any items left at the end could be donated to a local charity.

A swap would help students save money and find something new without spending anything. It would also encourage reuse, reduce waste and bring students together.

I hope the council will consider this idea.

Best wishes,
Alex

### 3. Comprobación
La composición tiene **142 palabras**, contando el asunto, el saludo y la despedida; queda dentro del límite de 120–150. Propone una actividad, explica cómo organizarla y justifica su utilidad.
preguntas.resultado: Propuesta de intercambio de ropa: 142 palabras; nota estimada: 3/3.
preguntas.criterios: Puntuación orientativa sobre 3 puntos: contenido y cumplimiento de la tarea, 1 punto; organización, cohesión y adecuación al formato y registro, 1 punto; corrección gramatical, vocabulario y ortografía, 1 punto. La respuesta propuesta alcanza 3/3 si se evalúa tal como está escrita.
